'''Assaf Friedler''' ({{Langx|he|אסף פרידלר}}; born 29 August 1971) is an [[Israelis|Israeli]] [[Organic chemistry|organic chemist]], [[biochemist]] and academic administrator. He is a professor at the Institute of Chemistry at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] and the director and chief executive officer of the Singapore–Hebrew University Alliance for Research and Enterprise (SHARE), the university's research and enterprise centre in Singapore.

== Early life and education ==

Friedler was born and raised in [[Haifa]], Israel. He studied chemistry at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], where he completed a Bachelor of Science degree in 1994.<ref name=education>{{cite journal |last1=Keinan |first1=Ehud |title=Welcome New Editorial Board Members! |journal=Israel Journal of Chemistry |date=February 2018 |volume=58 |issue=1–2 |pages=3–6 |doi=10.1002/ijch.201800015 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ijch.201800015 |language=en |issn=0021-2148}}</ref>

He subsequently began doctoral studies in [[organic chemistry]] at the Hebrew University under the supervision of Chaim Gilon. He completed his PhD in chemistry, with distinction, in 2000. In the same year, Friedler moved to the United Kingdom, where he was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] [[Centre for Protein Engineering]] in [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]] and worked in the laboratory of [[Sir Alan Fersht]].<ref name=education />

== Career ==

In 2004, Friedler joined the Institute of Chemistry at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] as a senior lecturer. He became an associate professor with tenure in 2009 and was appointed full professor in 2015.<ref name=hujiprofile>{{cite web |title=Assaf Friedler |url=https://friedlerlab.huji.ac.il/assaf-friedler |website=The Hebrew University of Jerusalem}}</ref> From 2005 to 2009, he headed the university's undergraduate chemistry–biology programme. He was head of the School of Chemistry.<ref>{{cite report |title=Sir Zelman Cowen Universities Fund Prize for Discovery in Medical Research |url=https://research.huji.ac.il/sites/default/files/mop/files/sir_zelman_cowen_brochure_final_for_print_-15_rgb_30.04.pdf |publisher=Authority for Research and Development, Hebrew University of Jerusalem |date=June 2015}}</ref>

Friedler served as vice rector of the Hebrew University from 2016 to 2020.<ref>{{cite report |title=Annual Report in Chemistry for 2018 |url=https://chemistry.huji.ac.il/sites/default/files/chemistry/files/annual_report_chemistry_2018_30-01-19.pdf |publisher=Institute of Chemistry, Hebrew University of Jerusalem}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://rector.huji.ac.il/moocteam|title=אודות לשכת הרקטור}}</ref> During the same period, he chaired the university's central student admissions committee.<ref name=hujiprofile /> He was dean of its Faculty of Science from 2020 to 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Deans throughout the years |url=https://en-science.huji.ac.il/dean-faculty |publisher=Hebrew University of Jerusalem}}</ref> He chaired the Hebrew University for the Youth from 2019 to 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Assaf Friedler |url=https://en.community-youth.huji.ac.il/people/assaf-friedler|publisher=Hebrew University of Jerusalem}}</ref>

In October 2024, Friedler became director and chief executive officer of SHARE, the Singapore–Hebrew University Alliance for Research and Enterprise.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Assaf Friedler |url=https://www.share-huj.edu.sg/staff/prof-assaf-friedler |website=Singapore–Hebrew University Alliance for Research and Enterprise |access-date=5 July 2026}}</ref>

== Research ==

Friedler's research is in [[chemical biology]], peptide chemistry, protein chemistry, [[biophysical chemistry]], and [[medicinal chemistry]]. It focuses on the use of peptides and peptide-based methods to study and inhibit [[protein–protein interaction|protein–protein interactions]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Katz |first1=Chen |last2=Levy-Beladev |first2=Liron |last3=Rotem-Bamberger |first3=Shahar |last4=Rito |first4=Tiago |last5=Rüdiger |first5=Stefan G. D. |last6=Friedler |first6=Assaf |title=Studying protein–protein interactions using peptide arrays |journal=Chemical Society Reviews |year=2011 |volume=40 |issue=5 |pages=2131–2145 |doi=10.1039/C0CS00029A |pmid=21243154}}</ref>, with a particular focus on interactions involving [[intrinsically disordered protein]] regions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Amartely |first1=Hadar |last2=David |first2=Ahuvit |last3=Lebendiker |first3=Mario |last4=Benyamini |first4=Hadar |last5=Izraeli |first5=Shai |last6=Friedler |first6=Assaf |title=The STIL protein contains intrinsically disordered regions that mediate its protein–protein interactions |journal=Chemical Communications |year=2014 |volume=50 |issue=40 |pages=5245–5247 |doi=10.1039/C3CC45096A |pmid=24022511}}</ref> His work has used synthetic, structural and biophysical approaches to investigate the molecular basis of these interactions and peptide-based methods to modulate them.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biology@CREATE Seminar |url=https://www.share-huj.edu.sg/news-press/biology-create-seminar |website=SHARE |date=30 May 2025 |access-date=5 July 2026}}</ref>

His research has examined interactions involving the tumour-suppressor protein [[p53]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Friedler |first1=Assaf |last2=Hansson |first2=Lars O. |last3=Veprintsev |first3=Dmitry B. |title=A peptide that binds and stabilizes p53 core domain: chaperone strategy for rescue of oncogenic mutants |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |year=2002 |volume=99 |issue=2 |pages=937–942 |doi=10.1073/pnas.241629998 |doi-access=free |pmid=11782540 |pmc=117409 }}</ref>, including its interactions with [[MDM2]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schon |first1=Oliver |last2=Friedler |first2=Assaf |last3=Bycroft |first3=Mark |last4=Freund |first4=Stefan M. V. |last5=Fersht |first5=Alan R. |title=Molecular mechanism of the interaction between MDM2 and p53 |journal=Journal of Molecular Biology |year=2002 |volume=323 |issue=3 |pages=491–501 * 2000 – [[Human Frontier Science Program]] Long-Term Postdoctoral Fellowship.<ref name=huji-evaluation>{{cite report |title=Institute of Chemistry Evaluation Report for MALAG |url=https://rector.huji.ac.il/files/self_evaluation_report_chemistry.pdf |publisher=Hebrew University of Jerusalem}}</ref>
* 2004 – Career Development Award, [[Human Frontier Science Program]]<ref name=huji-evaluation />
* 2007 – Starting Grant, [[European Research Council]]<ref>{{cite report |title=ERC Starting Grant Competition 2007 – Results |url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc_2007_stg_results_all%20domains.pdf |publisher=European Research Council |date=8 May 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Young chemists win share of ERC windfall |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/young-chemists-win-share-of-erc-windfall/3004354.article |website=Chemistry World |language=en}}</ref>
* 2013 – Rector's Prize for Excellence in Research and Teaching, [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]
* 2015 – Sir Zelman Cowen Universities Fund Prize for Discovery in Medical Research<ref>{{cite report |title=Sir Zelman Cowen Universities Fund Prize for Discovery in Medical Research 2015 |url=https://research.huji.ac.il/sites/default/files/mop/files/sir_zelman_cowen_brochure_final_for_print_-15_rgb_30.04.pdf |publisher=Authority for Research and Development, Hebrew University of Jerusalem |date=June 2015 |access-date=5 July 2026}}</ref>
* 2018 – Michael Milken Prize for Excellence in Teaching.
